title: Redwood Data Retention & PII Controls Demo - Tidewater Bank
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Tidewater Bank through data handling and retention controls in the Console and API. Main topics: logging redaction, PII detection, request storage toggle, per-tenant retention windows, KMS integration, deletion APIs, and audit logs. Customer concerned about regulatory retention windows, proof of deletion, and SSO access controls. Agreed next steps: send security whitepaper, share Dedicated pilot pricing, schedule SOC 2 deep-dive with Derek.
topics: audit logs and proof of deletion

Jonas to provision demo tenant with retention toggles for Tidewater test cluster (by 2026-03-18)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-14 15:00 PST - Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonas Patel (Redwood SE), Samantha Ruiz (CTO - Tidewater), Derek Lim (Security Engineer), Priya Nair (Platform Lead)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side, and Jonas is our SE. Today we're going to run through our data handling controls, specifically logging redaction, PII detection, and the request storage toggles in the Console and API.

[00:18] Samantha Ruiz: Great, thanks. Wanted to make sure we cover retention windows and proof of deletion, those are big for compliance.

[00:32] Jonas Patel: Absolutely, we'll demo the Console flow and then show the API calls. Quick note: transcription might mishear some acronyms, so apologies in advance, you'll see things like KV cash in the notes sometimes.

[00:45] Derek Lim: Haha, KV cash, okay. Let's start with high level \u2014 what options do we have for not storing requests or redacting sensitive fields at ingest?

[01:05] Jonas Patel: On Redwood you have three main levers. One, a request storage toggle at the tenant or route level that prevents storing raw request payloads. Two, automatic PII detection and redaction in logs and request store. Three, encryption + deletion APIs for revoke/erasures. We'll show the Console where you can flip these per-route.

[01:30] Maya Chen: And to add, we support per-tenant policy overrides for Dedicated and Private deployments, so for regulated customers you can set a strict retention window or disable storage entirely.

[01:45] Priya Nair: If we disable storage, does that impact model performance or caching? We rely on prefix caching for low latency.

[02:00] Jonas Patel: Good question. If you disable request storage, KV cache (sorry, KV cache) still functions for active sessions; we don't persist user-level request history for audits, but the runtime's KV cache remains in-memory for serving. For persistent prefix caching we have configurable TTLs that can be short for privacy-sensitive routes. There's a tradeoff between cache hit rate and data persistence.

[02:32] Samantha Ruiz: How granular can policies be? Per-route, per-model, per-environment?

[02:45] Jonas Patel: You can scope at route-level, which maps well to API endpoints, and at tenant-level for global defaults. In Dedicated/Private you can also configure per-model retention via policy files. We'll show the Console UI in a sec.

[03:05] Maya Chen: Quick run-through: we'll share a demo link to a tenant we prepped with three routes: /support-chat (default), /payments-redact (sensitive), and /analytics (low sensitivity). We'll flip the storage toggle and show logs.

[03:25] Jonas Patel: Starting screen share now \u2014 Console > Tenants > tidewater-demo. On the right you can see Data Handling. There's a toggle 'Store Requests' with options: On / Off / Redact-only. Redact-only stores metadata and redacted text.

[03:52] Derek Lim: When redaction runs, what detectors do you use? Is it regex only or ML-based entity detection?

[04:05] Jonas Patel: It's hybrid. We use pattern matching for structured values (card numbers, SSNs) plus an ML-based PII detector trained on common entities. You can supply custom regexes too, for internal PIDs. The ML detector flags tokens for redaction and you can preview the redacted output in the Console.

[04:35] Samantha Ruiz: Is the PII detector on the request stream or post-hoc? We need to make sure nothing is persisted unredacted even briefly.

[04:50] Jonas Patel: It runs synchronously in the ingest pipeline before any storage write. So if you have Store Requests = Off, we still run the detector for routing and moderation decisions but nothing is written. If Redact-only, we persist the redacted artifact.

[05:12] Priya Nair: Walk me through a deletion event \u2014 say a customer asks for all data about user X removed. How do we prove deletion?

[05:28] Maya Chen: We expose deletion APIs and audit logs. The deletion API returns a deletion token and we log the operation in the audit trail \u2014 who initiated it, timestamp, scope. For Dedicated/Private, we can provide a DB snapshot that shows the record was removed. We also have 'proof of deletion' where we can run a scan job and return a signed statement that no items matching the selector exist.

[06:00] Derek Lim: Signed statement \u2014 is that cryptographically signed? Can it be verified by a 3rd party?

[06:12] Jonas Patel: For customers who need that level, we integrate with HSM/KMS to sign artifacts. The signed proof can be independently verified against the public key. It's an add-on for enterprise plans but supported.

[06:30] Samantha Ruiz: KMS integrations \u2014 which providers? We use AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault.

[06:42] Jonas Patel: We support AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, and Vault via PKCS#11 or Transit. For Private deployments you can use an on-prem HSM.

[06:58] Maya Chen: Demo continues \u2014 toggling the /payments-redact route to Redact-only. Now I'll send a sample request.

[07:12] Jonas Patel: (typing) API call: POST /v1/generate route=payments-redact body {"card_number":"4111 1111 1111 1111","amount":"25.00","note":"customer DOB 1984-06-12"} \u2014 sending.

[07:30] Samantha Ruiz: Can you show the Console log line for that?

[07:35] Jonas Patel: Here: Log entry shows request id, time, route, and redacted payload: {"card_number":"<REDACTED_CARD>","amount":"25.00","note":"customer DOB <REDACTED_DATE>"}. We also show a confidence score for each redaction.

[07:52] Derek Lim: Confidence score \u2014 are there false positives? How do we tune?

[08:04] Jonas Patel: You can provide feedback via the Console \u2014 accept/reject redactions \u2014 which feeds into the model for your tenant. Also you can upload custom entity lists and regexes to minimize false positives.

[08:20] Priya Nair: For retention windows, what's the smallest granularity? Minutes? Hours?

[08:30] Jonas Patel: You can set TTLs down to minutes for ephemeral routes. Default policy is days. For compliance holds you can mark records under legal hold which prevents deletion until released.

[08:50] Samantha Ruiz: Legal hold \u2014 does that require Redwood to keep data longer than policy? We might need to show auditors.

[08:58] Maya Chen: Legal hold is tenant or object-scoped and is an override. When active, deletion APIs will raise an error for those items. The audit log shows who placed the hold and why.

[09:15] Jonas Patel: Switching to API view \u2014 there's a request param: storage=off|on|redact. Example: POST /v1/generate?storage=redact. We'll send an example and you can capture the network trace.

[09:35] Jonas Patel: (sends) Response returns request_id and redaction_summary. The server never returns the unredacted payload once redact mode is enabled.

[09:50] Derek Lim: If we need to rerun a prompt for debugging, is there an escape hatch? How do we reconcile debug needs with privacy?

[09:58] Jonas Patel: We have a 'retention-exempt' flag for internal debug sessions that requires explicit RBAC and SSO approval; it's logged as a privileged action and tied to an SSO assertion. It also requires a business justification that is recorded.

[10:18] Priya Nair: RBAC \u2014 can we map to our SAML groups? We need to limit who can flip retention toggles.

[10:28] Maya Chen: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC maps to roles. You can require MFA for any action that changes data handling.

[10:40] Samantha Ruiz: On audit logs \u2014 what do they retain? Do they contain PII?

[10:50] Jonas Patel: Audit logs are metadata-only by default: user, action, object id, timestamp. They don't include raw payloads unless you enable debug retention. Audit entries themselves are signed and stored in a WORM-backed store for the retention period you specify.

[11:10] Derek Lim: WORM-backed \u2014 is that configurable per region? We have EU data that needs to stay in EU.

[11:20] Jonas Patel: Yes, you can select data residency per tenant. For hosted we support region pinning; for Dedicated/Private you can deploy in the customer's VPC/region.

[11:38] Samantha Ruiz: Walk me through a scenario: PCI scope reduction. We don't want card numbers stored anywhere. How does Redwood help?

[11:50] Maya Chen: For PCI, recommend setting Store Requests=Off on any route that handles card data, use Redact-only when you need auditable redacted entries, and enforce TTLs and legal hold policies. Combine that with KMS and access controls
--only a small set of users can see redaction confirmations. This reduces scope because you won't have raw card data stored in logs.

[12:20] Jonas Patel: Also, we support tokenization integrations \u2014 Redwood can return a token in lieu of the raw value and the tokenization service is either customer-managed or via our partner tokenizers.

[12:35] Priya Nair: Tokenization would help, yes. Could you show the API response with tokenization?

[12:42] Jonas Patel: Sure, example: {"card_token":"tok_abc123","exp_month":6}. The raw is replaced server-side before storage.

[12:58] Samantha Ruiz: On the logs you showed earlier, can we get a CSV export for auditors?

[13:05] Jonas Patel: Yes, Console exports include redacted artifacts and audit logs; you can choose fields and time range. Exports are also signed and can be routed to S3 with a lifecycle policy.

[13:25] Derek Lim: About proofs of deletion \u2014 can we schedule routine scans and get weekly proofs?

[13:35] Jonas Patel: Yes, scheduled retention scans and signed manifests are supported. You can have them delivered to an S3 bucket or via API.

[13:50] Maya Chen: Let's demo a deletion: I'm removing a sample object id=abc-123 from the request store. (click) API call delete /v1/requests/abc-123. Response: {"status":"deleted","deletion_token":"del_20260314_9f"}.

[14:10] Jonas Patel: Now check audit log: shows deletion_token, actor=Maya Chen, tenant=tidewater-demo, and a SHA256 of the previous object for tamper evidence.

[14:30] Samantha Ruiz: SHA256 \u2014 so we keep a hash to prove prior existence but not the content?

[14:38] Jonas Patel: Correct. The hash is stored to prove the object existed and was removed; the content is not stored in plaintext.

[14:50] Priya Nair: Are hashes reversible? We need to ensure that hashes don't leak PII.

[14:58] Jonas Patel: We salt hashes with a tenant-specific secret before hashing, and the secret is stored in KMS so it's not derivable without keys.

[15:12] Derek Lim: Ok that helps. Another question \u2014 who in Redwood can access raw request data in hosted mode? Is it limited to SEs? We need a guarantee for audits.

[15:25] Maya Chen: Access is strictly controlled via RBAC and audited. By default, no Redwood engineer has access to customer raw payloads for tenants with Store Requests=Off or Redact-only. For Hosted accounts that enable debug retention, we require a written approval and perform access under an access window with recorded justification. All access is recorded in the audit log.

[15:50] Samantha Ruiz: If we move to Dedicated, can we host the data in our VPC so Redwood never sees the keys?

[15:58] Jonas Patel: Yes, Dedicated and Private modes are designed for that. Keys can be customer-managed and never accessible to Redwood. You can also run the control plane in a customer-managed subnet if needed.

[16:15] Maya Chen: Quick pivot to Optimize \u2014 there are suggestions to reduce token cost while maintaining privacy: aggressive prefix caching, model quantization, and route-level batching. But caching needs careful TTLs for privacy-sensitive routes. We can run workload analysis to recommend a profile.

[16:40] Priya Nair: Can Optimize simulate the privacy/cost trade-offs? A model that shows cost delta if we set TTL to 5m vs 1h?

[16:50] Jonas Patel: Yes, Optimize takes your usage patterns and recommends batching and TTLs that meet latency SLOs. It can also simulate expected token spend under various retention settings. We'll include a sample Optimize report in the follow-up.

[17:10] Samantha Ruiz: Sounds good. A question on juristictional holds \u2014 if regulators demand data for an investigation, how do you handle e-discovery while respecting our tenant controls?

[17:22] Jonas Patel: We have an e-discovery workflow: authorized legal requests go through a documented process, requiring Tidewater-approved admin to assent. We produce exports that respect redaction policies unless a lawful unredaction is legally mandated and you provide the appropriate court order; even then we require SSO-based approvals and log everything.

[17:48] Derek Lim: We're also curious about retention defaults for sandbox vs prod. Is there a way to force retention policies by environment?

[17:58] Jonas Patel: Environments map to tenants and you can enforce immutable policies in Dedicated via policy-as-code. For hosted, an account admin can lock policy settings to prevent devs from changing them.

[18:15] Maya Chen: Demo the policy-as-code view real quick. (shares) Here's a JSON policy that enforces store_requests=false for any route tagged pii=true and TTL=72h for logs. You can commit that and it applies via our control plane.

[18:40] Priya Nair: Nice. How do we roll that out without breaking existing routes? Any dry-run?

[18:50] Jonas Patel: We support a 'preview' apply which simulates changes and lists the affected objects. Use the canary rollout to apply to a subset of routes first.

[19:05] Samantha Ruiz: Back to redaction false positives \u2014 if a token like 555-55-5555 is identified but it's actually our internal employee id, what's the recovery?

[19:17] Jonas Patel: You can whitelist patterns or specific values per tenant. When whitelisted, redaction won't trigger. All whitelist changes are audited.

[19:30] Derek Lim: For the schedules we run, we'd like automated weekly proofs of deletion and monthly signed manifests. Can that be pushed to our S3 with cross-account access?

[19:42] Jonas Patel: Yes, we can push to your S3 via cross-account role. The manifest is signed and includes a checksum and scoped summary.

[19:55] Maya Chen: We're ~20 minutes in \u2014 any other big blockers from your side?

[20:02] Samantha Ruiz: Mainly two: need to see Dedicated pricing for a pilot; and Derek wants the SOC 2 & data flow diagrams.

[20:12] Maya Chen: We'll include the SOC 2 pack and an infra diagram that shows where keys and data live. Jonas will stand up a demo tenant with the toggles and the signed-manifest export.

[20:25] Jonas Patel: Quick show of the API swagger \u2014 endpoints for redaction config, deletion, audit export. Example: POST /v1/config/redaction {rules: [...]}. You can see schema and try it from the Console.

[20:50] Priya Nair: Are there rate limits or cost implications for running frequent scans and signed manifests?

[20:58] Jonas Patel: There's a small compute cost for signed scans, and we treat them as job requests. For pilot we can include limited scans; at scale we'll recommend a cadence that balances cost and assurance.

[21:15] Samantha Ruiz: Let's do the follow-ups then. We'll review the whitepaper and the demo tenant, run a small test, and then schedule the SOC 2 deep-dive.

[21:25] Derek Lim: Can Jonas send the API sample code? Preferably Python and curl examples.

[21:30] Jonas Patel: Absolutely, I'll attach samples in the follow-up.

[21:36] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps: Maya sends security pack and pricing; Jonas provisions demo tenant and sample API snippets; Tidewater to share retention policy. We'll aim for SOC 2 deep-dive week of 3/22.

[21:50] Samantha Ruiz: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the demo \u2014 felt thorough.

[21:55] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up.

[22:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mishears (KV cash) and truncated timestamps; speaker labels are accurate for the most part but may show generic labels in exported raw.
